Item text and item codes: S2 File 'Overall data - master file' (journal.pone.0261717.s003, XLSX, sha256 341263dd6c656bfee665e908b1a75f1a717d99991a76b2957ab1d0a608d4a772), sheet 'Codings of Questionnaire' (columns Questionnaire Number / Question / Abbreviation) and sheet 'Data Statement Sheet' header rows 1-2 (Q1..Q11 over EEL..ECT). Processing script data/srivani_2022_education4.py.
note: MAPPING (data_labels): the IRW item codes EEL..ECT are the source file's own abbreviations. The processing script renames Q1..Q11 to them via a hard-coded dict; that dict was checked against the Data Statement Sheet's second header row (Q1->EEL ... Q11->ECT, 11/11 identical) and against the Codings sheet's Questionnaire Number->Abbreviation columns (11/11), so the code-to-text tie is at the source, not inferred. TEXT: item_text is the Codings sheet's 'Question' column verbatim; it matches the administered S1 questionnaire PDF 11/11 (whitespace-insensitive; the only differences from a straight pdftotext string match were word-joins introduced by PDF extraction). The paper's Table 2 prints slightly edited wording for some statements (e.g. item 4 'caters to all age groups' needs', item 10 'to learn English'); the questionnaire/data-file wording was shipped instead. No instructions are printed on the questionnaire (heading 'Questionnaire', columns 'S. No.' / 'Statements'), so instructions is blank; instrument is named from that heading plus the study title printed on the form. OPTIONS: labels from the questionnaire's own printed codes (Strongly agree (2), Agree (1), Neutral (0)); only the three levels present in the live table are shipped for every item. Direction/labels confirmed against numbers: the S2 File's 'Cummulative Summary' sheet uses the same weights (2/1/0/-1/-2) and its per-item Strongly agree/Agree/Neutral/Disagree counts equal the raw Data Statement Sheet counts 44/44 cells; the live table's per-item counts of resp 2/1/0 equal the source's Strongly agree/Agree/Neutral counts 33/33 cells (e.g. EEL 63/82/0, ELN 60/56/22, ECT 58/77/6), and the sheet's mean formula reproduces the paper's Table 2 means (item 1 (63*2+82)/145 = 1.434). The paper's Methods text says 'strongly agree as level 1 ... strongly disagree as level 5', which contradicts both the form and the data file; the form's printed codes are what the data use. RESPONSE-DATA DEFECT (not an item-text issue): the source records 20 responses coded -1, which the questionnaire labels 'Disagree' (ELN 7, LET 2, ELS 3, TDE 4, ECT 4; the Cummulative Summary sheet counts them as Disagree with weight -1). data/srivani_2022_education4.py drops them as 'data-entry errors / sentinel values' on the premise that the scale has no negative code, so the live table has 1575 rows instead of 1595 and those five items lose their Disagree responses; this biases those items upward. No respondent used Strongly disagree (-2). Paper Table 2's Disagree counts (items 8-11: 1/2/3/1) also differ from the file's (2/3/4/4). RIGHTS: researcher-designed questionnaire ('The questionnaire for the students was prepared by the researchers, which comprised 11 statements'), published in a CC BY article and its supplements; no third-party instrument, no restriction found. LANGUAGE: administered in English ('eleven questions formulated in the English language'), so no language/_translated columns. STEP 3b: clean - 11 items, 145 ids, content matches the 11-statement students' questionnaire; the paper's other measure (pre/post English assessment, Table 1) is not this table.
public_note: The questionnaire offered five options (Strongly agree 2 to Strongly disagree -2), but the response table omits the 20 'Disagree' (-1) responses recorded in the source file for items ELN, LET, ELS, TDE and ECT, so only the Neutral, Agree and Strongly agree options appear here
